5.5. Constraints #

5.5.1. Check Constraints
5.5.2. Unique Constraints

Data types limit the kind of value a column can hold. Constraints add further rules that the stored rows must satisfy.

5.5.1. Check Constraints #

A check constraint requires that a value satisfies a Boolean expression.

CREATE TABLE items (
    price numeric CHECK (price > 0)
);

Note

A check constraint is evaluated only for the row being inserted or updated.

Examples #

The first example limits a numeric column to positive values.

5.5.2. Unique Constraints #

A unique constraint ensures that the values in a column are distinct among all rows.

Note

Two null values are not considered equal unless the constraint says so.

Tip

Name the constraint to make error messages easier to read; see CREATE TABLE.

Examples #

The second example declares a unique pair of columns.
